currentContext.expansion: The annual report describes no named capacity-expansion project, greenfield plant or commissioning timeline. The Board's Report states in a single line that "The total capital expenditure incurred by the Company during the financial year under review was Rs 574.49 Lakhs", without attributing it to any specific project or division. Expansion intent is expressed only as market development rather than capacity build-out: the Building Material Division is undertaking initiatives to strengthen its marketing and distribution network to improve market penetration and expand customer reach, and plans to introduce high-end waterproofing systems; the Industrial Gear Box vertical under the 'IC TORQUE DRIVE' brand, introduced in line with the 'Make in India' initiative, is being grown by expanding the product range; and the Heavy Engineering Division is focused on strengthening execution capabilities, improving operational efficiencies and expanding customer reach. The Company operates manufacturing facilities at Baidyabati, Nagpur, Aurangabad and Ajmer with a corporate office at Kolkata, and has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture company. Energy conservation initiatives are being implemented in a phased manner.

risks.risk: Dependence on capital expenditure by core industries (steel, mining, cement, power, infrastructure)
risks.note: Demand is largely dependent on investments in core industries; any slowdown in economic activity, reduction in capital expenditure or deferment of projects by customers may adversely impact order inflow, execution cycle and overall business performance. During FY26 demand from these sectors remained uneven due to deferment of customer capex and delays in industrial projects.

risks.risk: Order execution risk - projects shelved or slowed even when orders are in hand
risks.note: Management states that a large number of new projects got shelved and even those under execution faced major slowdown, so that despite having orders in hand these could not be executed. The Board specifically monitors order execution risk. Revenue conversion therefore depends on customer project schedules rather than order book alone.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility, particularly steel, and input cost inflation
risks.note: The Company faces volatility in prices of steel and other key raw materials and inflationary trends; the increase in input costs is described as continuing to remain a major challenge. Higher operating costs without growth in sales was the stated reason for the decline in operating margin, net margin and return on net worth in FY26.

risks.risk: Competitive pricing pressure including from low-cost imports
risks.note: Intense competition from domestic as well as international manufacturers, including low-cost imports, exerts pressure on pricing, margins and market share. Competitive pricing pressure is also one of the risks the Board reviewed during the year.

risks.risk: Receivables and working capital / liquidity management
risks.note: Managing receivables and ensuring timely collection of dues from customers remain important areas of focus given the nature of the business and the project execution cycle; working capital management and liquidity constraints are listed among the key risks faced by the Company.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and logistics constraints
risks.note: Supply chain disruptions are named among the key risks; during FY26 logistics constraints and pressure on supply chains impacted operational efficiencies and project execution timelines.

The Company cites fluctuations in foreign exchange rates among the challenges it faces, relevant given imports/technology licences from Bauer (Germany) and CAPA (Spain) and sales to customers overseas.

Changes in regulatory policies are listed among the key risks; the cautionary statement further flags changes in government regulations, tax laws and the political environment as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from expectations.

Two of the three divisions run on licensed technology - geared motors under licence from Bauer, Germany and advanced dry mortar under a licence agreement with CAPA, Spain - so the product platforms in those verticals rest on continuing third-party technical collaborations.
